'''''Erica canariensis''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Ericaceae]], [[Native species|native]] to [[Madeira]] and the [[Canary Islands]].<ref name=POWO_77194907-1/> ''Erica canariensis'' was distinguished from ''[[Erica arborea]]'' by [[Salvador Rivas-Martínez]] and co-authors in 2011.<ref name=Riva11/> The distinction is not accepted by all sources.

==Description==
''Erica canariensis'' resembles ''E. arborea''. Its differences include being an upright tree 6 to 9 m tall with a trunk up to 2 m in diameter. Young branches are densely covered with mainly simple hairs of variable lengths. The leaves are more-or-less flat, only slightly inrolled (revolute). The [[inflorescence]]s have an elongated pyramidal shape. The [[petal|corolla]] is up to 5 mm long, shortly bell-shaped.<ref name=Riva11/> Its white bell-shaped flowers distinguish it from the other species found in the Canaries, ''[[Erica platycodon]]''.<ref name=Flora/>

==Taxonomy==
''Erica canariensis'' was first described in 2011,<ref name=IPNI_77194907-1/> when it was distinguished from ''E. arborea'' by Salvador Rivas Martínez and co-authors.<ref name=Riva11/> {{As of|2025|October}}, the distinction is accepted by [[Plants of the World Online]],<ref name=POWO_77194907-1/> but not by other taxonomic databases, such as [[World Flora Online]], which treats it as a synonym of ''E. arborea''.<ref name=WFO_1000035207/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Erica canariensis'' is native to Madeira and the Canary Islands, where it is found in shady forests and thickets. The [[holotype]] was found on the north side of [[Teide]] in Tenerife at an altitude of around 2,100 m.<ref name=Riva11/>
